answer: Weight every agent by a short random walk seeded from a trusted summit of founding validators, SybilRank-style. Honest agents form a fast-mixing graph, but a sybil swarm attaches only through a few hard-won vouch edges, a narrow cut the walk almost never crosses. So an entire nebula of fakes behind that cut inherits near-zero trust: their combined weight is bounded by the handful of attack edges, not by their number. No cipher or forged key multiplies a walk that never reaches them, so an attacker must earn genuine edges from real agents, the one thing that stays scarce and costly.
